meta.case_name: Switch Room and Bulb Room – Logic Puzzle

prompt.context: This is a logic/brain-teaser question. There are two rooms: The Switch Room and the Bulb Room. In the Switch Room there are three switches (1, 2, 3); all switches are marked On and Off and are originally in the Off position. In the Bulb Room there are three light bulbs (A, B, C). You must match each switch to the light bulb it controls.
prompt.question: You start in the Switch Room and may do whatever you want with the three switches. Then you step into the Bulb Room. Without going back to the Switch Room, how do you figure out which switch controls which light bulb?

clarifying_info.q: Are the light bulbs standard incandescent bulbs that generate heat when on?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, you may assume they are standard incandescent bulbs that heat up when on.

clarifying_info.q: Can I use any sense — touch, sight — when in the Bulb Room?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, you can observe and touch the bulbs.

clarifying_info.q: How long may I leave switches on before entering the Bulb Room?
clarifying_info.a: As long as you like — time is not restricted.

framework: Recognize the constraint: 3 unknowns but only 2 observable binary states (on/off) unless extra information is introduced
Identify the hidden variable: heat. An incandescent bulb retains warmth for a few minutes after being switched off
Design a protocol that encodes three distinct states: always-on, briefly-on-then-off, always-off
Map each state to a unique bulb observation (bright/on, dark-but-warm, dark-and-cold)

questions.prompt: Describe the exact sequence of switch actions you take in the Switch Room before walking to the Bulb Room.
questions.guidance: Turn on Switch 1 and Switch 2. Wait a few minutes (e.g., 3 minutes) so that both bulbs heat up. Then turn off Switch 2, leaving Switch 1 on and Switch 3 off. Walk into the Bulb Room.

questions.prompt: Once you are in the Bulb Room, how do you identify which bulb corresponds to which switch?
questions.guidance: Observe and touch all three bulbs. One bulb is lit (on) — it is controlled by Switch 1 (left on). Two bulbs are dark: touch them. One dark bulb is warm — it is controlled by Switch 2 (turned on for ~3 minutes then turned off). The remaining dark, cold bulb is controlled by Switch 3 (never turned on). This exploits heat as the extra input needed to distinguish three states from two observables.

brainstorming.prompt: The same page poses two additional brain-teaser questions. For each, list the key answers a strong candidate would give.

categories.name: NPV boxes question — questions to ask before choosing a box
ideas: What is the discount rate used in each NPV calculation?
What is the time frame and period length of each cash-flow projection?
What is the range / distribution of possible outcomes for each package?
What is the liquidity of each package (how quickly can the value be realized)?

categories.name: Why are manholes round?
ideas: A round cover cannot fall into a circular hole regardless of orientation — a square or rectangular cover could be tilted and dropped in diagonally
Round covers can be moved by rolling, requiring no heavy lifting
A circle maximizes the opening area relative to the perimeter (material cost and weight), making it the most material-efficient shape

recommendation: For the switch-bulb puzzle: turn on switches 1 and 2, wait ~3 minutes, turn off switch 2, then enter the Bulb Room; the lit bulb = switch 1, the warm-dark bulb = switch 2, the cold-dark bulb = switch 3
The key insight is using a physical property (heat/temperature) as a third observable state to resolve three unknowns with what initially appears to be only two binary observations
risks: Assumes incandescent (heat-generating) bulbs; solution does not work with LED bulbs which do not retain significant heat
Requires waiting long enough for bulbs to heat up and short enough that the warm bulb has not fully cooled
next_steps: Generalize: ask the interviewer whether a version with four bulbs and four switches is solvable (it is, by adding a second heat-exposure interval)
